questions.question: You run `ls out.txt missing.txt 2>&1 > wrong.txt`. Where does the error message about missing.txt go?
options: To the terminal, because stderr was pointed at stdout's old target before stdout moved to the file
Nowhere; the command fails before running
questions.explanation: Redirections are processed left to right. 2>&1 copies where FD 1 points at that moment (the terminal); only afterwards is FD 1 moved to wrong.txt. Use > wrong.txt 2>&1 to capture both.

questions.question: Why does `sort names.txt > names.txt` leave names.txt empty?
options: sort deletes its input file after reading it
The shell truncates names.txt when setting up the redirection, before sort reads it
sort cannot write to files, only to the terminal
The file is locked while sort runs
questions.explanation: The shell opens and truncates the output file before the command starts, so sort reads an already-empty file. sort -o names.txt names.txt is the safe form.

questions.question: Why does `sudo echo "10.0.0.5 db.internal" >> /etc/hosts` fail with Permission denied?
options: echo is not allowed to run under sudo
The redirection is performed by your own non-root shell before sudo runs
questions.explanation: Only echo runs as root; the file is opened by your shell. Piping into sudo tee -a /etc/hosts lets a root process open the file.

questions.question: Without pipefail, what is the exit status of `ls missing.txt 2>/dev/null | wc -l`?
options: 0, because a pipeline reports the status of its last command
questions.explanation: By default the pipeline's status is wc's, which succeeded. With set -o pipefail the failing ls status (2) is reported instead.
